name_note: GTDB places this species in Coprococcus_A, a split of the classical genus; a recent classification proposes the name Pseudocoprococcus catus for the same organism.

sentences.text: Coprococcus catus is an intestinal lactate-utilizing bacterium that converts lactate to short-chain fatty acids, including butyrate.
A genome-mining study annotated the propanediol utilization compartment in Coprococcus catus alongside other lactate utilizers.
A prospective study of shotgun metagenomes from 4,685 Swedish adults, of whom 383 developed type 2 diabetes, reported Coprococcus catus among three species associated with lower risk.
A genome-based classification concluded that Coprococcus catus differs from Coprococcus sensu stricto and placed it in a new genus as Pseudocoprococcus catus.
